before_ingredients_html:
Simplified version

Use peeled, deveined raw frozen shrimp thawed in the fridge. Skip herbs and chilli; garlic, butter and lemon are enough.

intro_html: Big shrimp in garlic butter with pul biber (mild red-pepper flakes). Planned for Göcek, Turkey · 24 October–around 7 November 2026. Also works in a home kitchen. See the seasonal shopping and supplier guide.

notes.html:
• Make the core ingredient list first.
  • Optional additions are separate; each is called out where it enters.
  • Quantities serve two.
  • Cook meat and seafood just before eating; keep dairy and raw ingredients refrigerated at 0–4 °C.
  • Prep vegetables before raw meat or use a separate board and clean tools.

steps.body_html:
• Check every shrimp for shell fragments and the dark back vein.
  • If needed, make a shallow cut along the back and lift the vein out.
  • Pat thoroughly dry, then season.
  • Keep refrigerated until the pan is hot.
steps.title: Dry the shrimp

steps.body_html:
• Heat olive oil and half the butter over medium-high heat in a 26 cm pan.
  • Add shrimp in a single layer.
  • Cook 1–2 minutes until the underside turns pink, then turn.
  • If crowded, sear half, transfer to a clean plate, then sear the second half, reserving pan fat between batches.
  • Return both batches only for the short garlic-butter finish in the next step.
steps.title: Sear in one layer

steps.body_html:
• Lower to medium-low; add the remaining butter, garlic and optional chilli.
  • Cook 1–2 minutes more, stirring the butter around the shrimp.
  • Garlic should stay pale gold.
  • Check the thickest shrimp is 63 °C and opaque through the centre; large shrimp may need longer.
steps.title: Add garlic without burning it

steps.body_html:
• Turn off the heat and stir in lemon.
  • Add optional parsley, spoon the butter over the shrimp and eat immediately with optional bread.
  • Shrimp should be juicy, not tightly curled and rubbery.
steps.title: Finish with lemon
